answer_1.quote: To systematically study how LLMs handle implicit misinformation, we introduce ECHOMIST, a carefully curated benchmark to measure how LLMs ECHO back (i.e., detect, correct, or amplify) MISinformaTion hidden within seemingly innocuous queries.
answer_1.outputs: model responses to user queries containing implicit misinformation

answer_2.quote: We design a 5-point Likert scale rating to capture three key aspects: (1) the model's ability to detect implicit misinformation, (2) its tendency to reinforce or correct false claims, and (3) the accuracy and adequacy of any correction, assessed against the reference explanations provided in ECHOMIST...

answer_3.quote: To evaluate model responses on a large scale, we adopt an automated LLM-as-a-judge method. We enhance the evaluation prompt with four key components: (1) the query, (2) the false claim which tests the model's detection capability, (3) the explanation, serving as the gold reference to assess whether model responses accurately and adequately correct the false claim, and (4) the detailed definition of our metric.
criteria: reinforcement or correction of false claim

answer_4.quote: To assess the reliability of our evaluation method, we randomly selected a subset of 70 queries from our dataset and had two human annotators (two Ph.D. students) independently rate the model responses according to our 5-point rating criteria.
answer_4.guideline: the 5-point rating criteria defined in the paper, including whether the model detects the false claim, corrects it, and provides an accurate explanation
criteria: reinforcement or correction of false claim
